transcript.text: I need to flag a critical IT issue for tomorrow's remote instruction plan. Our learning-management-system authentication will be offline for scheduled maintenance from 8:00 to 11:00 a.m. tomorrow. I confirmed the maintenance window with the vendor today, but the vendor notice hasn't been attached to the remote-day draft yet. Since the draft plan schedules instruction through the LMS beginning at 8:00 a.m., we have a direct conflict. Instead, instructional files must be distributed by email as downloadable PDFs and made available for printing by 7:30 a.m. tomorrow.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, Mr. Brooks. That's a critical conflict — if the LMS is down from 8:00 to 11:00 a.m., we can't have instruction beginning through that system at 8:00 a.m. Your proposed alternative of distributing instructional files by email as downloadable PDFs, available by 7:30 a.m., seems like a reasonable workaround. Before I finalize the plan, I want to hear from the other briefing areas as well — transportation on meal delivery, nursing on health support, and family engagement on communication — so I can approve a complete remote instruction day plan that addresses instructional delivery, meal access, health support, and family communication all at once.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical health support issue for tomorrow's remote instruction plan. The district nurse coverage plan requires the usual school voicemail to be replaced entirely by a staffed nurse hotline from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. tomorrow for students who need medication or urgent health guidance during remote instruction. Voicemail is not to be used as a fallback or co-equal channel during this window. I confirmed the coverage roster this afternoon, but it has not yet been entered in the plan. This directly conflicts with the current draft, which directs health questions to the usual school voicemail.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical transportation issue for tomorrow's remote instruction plan. My department's storm route review, completed this afternoon, found that no buses can safely travel tomorrow. This directly conflicts with the current draft plan, which sends meals by regular bus routes. Instead, meals must be made available for on-site pickup at North Campus and South Campus from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. The route review results have not yet been added to the operations briefing packet.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical family communication and access issue for tomorrow's remote instruction plan. My family outreach confirmations, completed this week, show that 38 households lack reliable internet access. Those households need printed learning packets plus bilingual phone check-ins in Spanish and Somali. This directly conflicts with the current draft plan, which assumes families can use digital materials. The family-access summary is still being compiled and has not yet been added to the draft plan. Given Mr. Brooks's point that the LMS will be down from 8:00 to 11:00 a.m., this access gap is even more urgent — these 38 households will be unable to participate at all without printed packets and direct phone outreach.
